findings.title: order mixin uses wrong value for old box-model ordinal-group properties
findings.body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based, while the standard `order` property is 0-based. The mixin passes `$val` directly to both, so `@include order(2)` produces `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 2` (which means "second position" in old syntax) but `order: 2` (which means "after two other groups" in standard syntax). The old prefixes should use `$val + 1` to produce equivalent visual ordering. This causes incorrect element ordering in browsers that only support the old box model (e.g., older Safari/iOS).

findings.title: -ms-align-items is not a valid CSS property
findings.body: The property `-ms-align-items` does not exist. The correct IE/Edge prefixed property for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line is dead code that will be silently ignored by all browsers, but it may mislead future maintainers into thinking IE alignment is handled by this line.

findings.title: align-items mixin does not map values for old vendor prefixes
findings.body: The old `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties use different keywords than standard `align-items` for some values: `flex-start` should become `start` and `flex-end` should become `end`. The mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim to all prefixes, so it will silently fail if called with `flex-start` or `flex-end`. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline` (which happen to be identical across specs), but the mixin is now a public utility that will break for future callers using other values.

findings.title: Removing .title float rule may break header layout for elements that still depend on it
findings.body: The diff removes `.title { float: left; }` from `.d-header` and replaces the parent `.contents` with flexbox. However, if any child elements within `.title` (or `.title` itself in certain templates/plugins) rely on the float to establish a block formatting context or to position sibling elements, they will now behave differently. More critically, `.title` is no longer explicitly styled at all—if it contains inline content that previously relied on the float to size correctly, it may now collapse or overflow in the flex container. Verify that `.title` renders correctly as a flex item without any explicit display or sizing rules.

findings.title: Removing bullet badge margin-top in extra-info-wrapper may cause vertical misalignment
findings.body: The rule `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` was removed and replaced with `line-height: 1.5` on the parent. The `line-height` increase affects all inline content in the wrapper, not just the bullet badge, and may not produce the same vertical offset for the bullet dot specifically. This could cause a visual regression where bullet category badges in the extra-info (docked header) appear misaligned relative to the title text.
